<description>
If a flush that prunes block files fails before the block index write, the files are already marked pruned in memory, but `setFilesToPrune` is a local in `FlushStateToDisk()`. The next successful flush writes the pruned file info and never deletes the blk/rev files. Only `ScanAndUnlinkAlreadyPrunedFiles()` deletes them, at the next startup.

This is number 7 of ryanofsky's [post-merge review of #35714](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#pullrequestreview-5697890316). The block file flush failure from #35714 and the blocks directory `CheckDiskSpace()` failure both return before that write.

I worked on this because it lets me test my kernel pruning refactor (for #35627 and kernel-node/kernel-node#111) against the issue he describes. The refactor moves the flush, block index write and file deletion that a pruning flush runs from `FlushStateToDisk()` into `WriteBlockStorage()`, and no unit test ran that sequence in prune mode. I rebased my refactor onto this branch and they pass.

The first three commits are test the current behavior for a flush after a failed one writes what was skipped, but a failed prune flush still leaves its files on disk after a retry.

The last commit keeps the selected files in `BlockManager` and deletes them after the next block index write. If that write fails they are dropped with the dirty entries, which means a file is only deleted once it is marked pruned on disk. Pending files don't force a write. The next flush that writes deletes them.

The disk-space failure and automatic pruning take the same path but have no test. Neither does the `FindNextBlockPos()` line that drops a file from the pending set when a block is written to it, which can happen after an assumeutxo snapshot validates.

I will be opening follow-ups as drafts based on top of this shortly.
</description>

<commits>
24ad36d929 test: apply BlockManager args in test fixtures

Without this, -prune and -fastprune in extra_args have no effect.

2334d27a24 test: check flush retry after failure

Move the blk file aside instead of deleting it, so it can be restored.

108d7ff03c test: characterize a failed prune flush

The pruned blk/rev files are not deleted, even after a later flush
succeeds.

d224fb8721 validation: delete pruned files on a later flush

Files selected for pruning were kept in a local, so a failed flush left
them on disk until the next startup.

Keep them in BlockManager and delete them after the next block index
write. Take them with the dirty entries, which WriteBlockIndexDB() drops
even if the write fails. Drop a file from the set once a block is
written to it.

Pending files wait for the next periodic, forced or shutdown flush
rather than forcing one, which would retry a failing write on every
block.
</commits>
